evals.prompt: This code works but has three layers of wrappers around one function. Clean it up.
evals.expected_output: The reply names the complexity, checks why each layer exists, removes one layer at a time, runs the full suite after each, and does not change behaviour.
expectations: The reply names a specific complexity, not a vague 'clean up'.
The reply checks the history or usage before removing a layer.
One change is made at a time with the full suite run after each.
Behaviour is unchanged; if a new test is added, it passes on both the old and new code.

evals.prompt: Remove the feature flag for the invite flow; it has been there for months.
evals.expected_output: The reply checks whether the flag is still used before removing it and stops or asks if it is, because removing a live flag changes behaviour.
expectations: The reply checks the flag's usage and history before removing it.
The reply refuses to remove a live flag without deciding the behaviour.
The reply does not treat the cleanup as behaviour-preserving if it is not.
